_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 12: AAOmega (id 'aaomega')
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote; DERIVED = arithmetic done here; EFFECTIVE = none used; INFERRED = a reading not stated; MEASURED = read from a figure with a stated scale; NOT FOUND = gap.
_meta.status: in operation since 2006 (CCDs replaced 2014, same format); no '(design)' tag

S16.cite: Saunders, W. 2016, Proc. SPIE 9908, 96, 'Very fast transmissive spectrograph designs for highly multiplexed fiber spectroscopy' (2016SPIE.9908E..96S; arXiv:1607.07721): the Hector design contrasted with AAOmega's obstructed collimator and cameras

S12.cite: Saunders, W. 2012, Proc. SPIE 8446, 54, 'A fast new catadioptric design for fiber-fed spectrographs' (2012SPIE.8446E..54S; arXiv:1207.7009): AAOmega design intent

L02.cite: Lewis, I. J., et al. 2002, MNRAS 333, 279, 'The Anglo-Australian Observatory 2dF facility' (2002MNRAS.333..279L; arXiv:astro-ph/0202175): the 2dF positioner, corrector, fibers (Table 1); the retired 2dF spectrographs

S10.cite: Sharp, R. & Birchall, M. N. 2010, PASA 27, 91, 'Optimal Extraction of Fibre Optic Spectroscopy' (2010PASA...27...91S; arXiv:0912.0558): AAOmega MOS mode, fiber pitch, PSF

H13.cite: Hopkins, A. M., et al. 2013, MNRAS 430, 2047, 'Galaxy And Mass Assembly (GAMA): spectroscopic analysis' (2013MNRAS.430.2047H; arXiv:1301.7127): the 580V/385R, 5700 A dichroic setup, coverage, dispersion, R

D11.cite: Driver, S. P., et al. 2011, MNRAS 413, 971, 'Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA): survey diagnostics and core data release' (2011MNRAS.413..971D; arXiv:1009.0614): 580V + 385R, 5700 A dichroic, coverage, resolution

D10.cite: Drinkwater, M. J., et al. 2010, MNRAS 401, 1429, 'The WiggleZ Dark Energy Survey: survey design and first data release' (2010MNRAS.401.1429D; arXiv:0911.4246): the 570 and 670 nm dichroics, 580V + 385R, Table 6

aaomega.title: AAT AAOmega: bench-mounted dual-beam fiber spectrograph fed by 2dF (392 fibers, 140 um, f/3.5), f/3.15 Schmidt collimator (190 mm beam), VPH gratings, f/1.3 articulating Schmidt cameras, 2 x 2k x 4k E2V CCDs of 15 um
aaomega.aperture_handling: D = 3.893 m (WD85), f/3.5 at the 2dF corrector; the explorer enters the fibers at the collimator's f/3.15 (virtual convention).
aaomega.collimator: Schmidt (mirror + correctors); ON-AXIS, INFERRED from obstruction-loss statements (no sentence, no figure): colTilt 0 (deploy gate: the user decides)

parameters.quote: D = 3893mm (AAT) | 3.9m AAT f/3.3 Prime focus
parameters.note: Same D as the explorer's AAT UHRF presets (3.893 m). The AAT's focal ratio at 2dF is the corrector's f/3.5 (next row).

parameters.parameter: 2dF corrector focal ratio and image scale
parameters.value: f/3.5; 67 um per arcsec (14.9 arcsec/mm)
parameters.quote: Corrector focal ratio f/3.5 | Image scale 67µm/arcsec
parameters.note: DERIVED check: 3.5 x 3893 mm = 13.62 m, 206 265 / 13 625 = 15.14 arcsec/mm = 66.1 um/arcsec (the printed 67 um/arcsec is 1.4% larger). The bare prime focus is f/3.3 (Table 1); the corrector sets 3.5. The input beam of every fiber is therefore f/3.5, which FRD and the corrector's non-telecentricity (up to 4 deg) widen to the f/3.15 the collimator accepts.

parameters.value: 392 science + 8 guide fibers per slit (400 slots); core 140 um, cladding 168 um, 38 m long
parameters.quote: The Polymicro Broadband fibres∗ have a nominal core diameter of 140um, cladding diameter 168um | 392 science fibre spectra | eight missing spectra where the guide fibres would be
parameters.note: INFERRED from the pair: the 'eight missing spectra' (Sec. 6) are the eight guide-fiber slots of a 400-slot slit. Fiber run 38 m (SH06 Sec. 2.1: 'replacement of the 8m fibre run with the 38m run'); the 2dF fibers had the same 140 um core (L02 Sec. 3.4: 'core diameter 140 µm'). Each 2dF field plate carries 400 fibers; the slit takes one plate at a time.

parameters.value: 2.1 arcsec mean (2.16 at the field center, 2.0 at the edge)
parameters.quote: corresponding to an average diameter of 2.1 arcsec on the sky | Fibre size on sky (mean) 2.1 arcsec
parameters.note: ALT D10 Sec. 4.1: 'The angular size of each fibre on the sky is 2 arc seconds'. DERIVED: 140 um / 67 um per arcsec = 2.09 arcsec.

parameters.parameter: Fiber input and output focal ratios
parameters.value: input f/3.5 (corrector); collimator accepts f/3.15
parameters.quote: Corrector focal ratio f/3.5 | f/3.15 Schmidt collimator
parameters.note: The explorer's virtual convention: F = 3.15 (the collimator's ratio, the beam the fibers must fill), core angle = 140 um / (3.15 x 3893 mm) = 2.355 arcsec, entered as the slit of equal line width sqrt(3)/2 x 2.355 = 2.039 arcsec (DERIVED; as BOSS, DESI, LAMOST). L02 (for the retired 2dF spectrographs, the same f/3.15 collimator speed) states the intent: the collimator 'slightly oversized compared to the prime focus corrector focal ratio of f/3.5, to allow for some focal ratio degradation'. The fiber output ratio itself is NOT FOUND for AAOmega.

parameters.parameter: Number of spectra on the detector (nObj)
parameters.value: 392 (400 slots; 8 empty guide slots)
parameters.quote: eight missing spectra where the guide fibres would be | 392 science fibres are deployed on astronomical targets
parameters.note: nObj = 392 for MOS (SPIRAL: 512 fibers, KOALA: 1000 lenslets, Secs. below; not entered).

parameters.value: ~10 pixels (150 um)
parameters.quote: the fibre pitch, of ∼10 pixels
parameters.note: DERIVED: 392 + 8 = 400 slots x 10 px x 15 um = 60 mm of the 61.4 mm 4096-px spatial axis; the 145 mm slit (SH06) demagnified by f_cam/f_col = 0.4127 is 59.8 mm. Consistent.

parameters.quote: The design has a 145mm fibre slit
parameters.note: With a field lens gelled to the slitlets ('telecentric (or more correctly, pupil-centric)'). 90 slitlets make up the full slit (SH06 Sec. 5.4).

parameters.value: all-Schmidt: f/3.15 spherical Schmidt collimator, with one corrector plate per arm after the dichroic
parameters.quote: an f/3.15 Schmidt collimator, incorporating a dichroic beam-splitter | incorporating a dichroic beam-splitter upstream of the corrector (this necessitates two correctors but minimises pupil relief)
parameters.note: Whether the mirror is the explorer's 'mirror' collimator: a Schmidt collimator is a reflecting (spherical mirror) collimator with a corrector plate; the papers do not say 'mirror' in so many words. INFERRED: col 'mirror' (the one-corrector-per-arm detail is not representable).

parameters.quote: Pupil size is 190mm, determined by the competing demands of cost, obstruction losses, and maximum resolution
f/3.15 Schmidt collimator | Pupil size is 190mm
parameters.note: DERIVED: 3.15 x 190 mm = 598.5 mm. Not stated as a length in the sources saved here (the Smith et al. 2004 and Saunders et al. 2004 SPIE papers, behind the SPIE paywall, give the prescription). ALT: the retired 2dF spectrographs used a 150 mm beam at f/3.15 = 472.5 mm (L02 Sec. 3.5), so the focal ratio is a carry-over.

parameters.value: ON-AXIS (Schmidt; the slit stands in the returning beam), INFERRED; no sentence states it
parameters.loc: SH06 abstract and Sec. 2.3; S16 Secs. 2 and 8; S14 Sec. 1
parameters.quote: determined by the competing demands of cost, obstruction losses, and maximum resolution | AAOmega [7] suffers from complex and variable diffractive blazes, imperfectly understood but clearly caused by the detector and spider in the beam. Hence a decision was taken to have a collimator with unobstructed pupil. An off-axis Schmidt collimator works fine | Classic Schmidt designs suffer from obstruction losses caused by the detector
parameters.note: VERDICT: the evidence is indirect, from three papers by the instrument's designer. (1) SH06: the pupil size trades 'obstruction losses' against resolution, so the pupil is obstructed. (2) S16 (Hector, which chose 'a collimator with unobstructed pupil' and an off-axis Schmidt 'by contrast', and says AAOmega's diffractive blazes are caused by 'the detector and spider in the beam'): the 'detector' obstruction is in the cameras; the slit-and-slitlet 'spider' obstruction is the collimator's. (3) The retired 2dF spectrographs had an off-axis Maksutov collimator 'with no central obstruction' (L02 Sec. 3.5), which AAOmega replaced with a Schmidt. A classical Schmidt collimator is on-axis by construction (slit at the focus on the mirror's axis, in front of the mirror). No drawing or sentence confirms the slit in the returning beam; the Smith 2004 and Saunders 2004 SPIE layout figures would. Recommended colTilt 0 (the user decides).

parameters.value: in the collimated beam, upstream of the per-arm correctors
parameters.quote: incorporating a dichroic beam-splitter upstream of the corrector (this necessitates two correctors but minimises pupil relief)
parameters.note: Split type for web/arms.js: 'collimated' (the dichroic stands in the collimated beam after the shared slit and collimator; each arm then has its own corrector, grating, camera and detector).

parameters.parameter: Camera type, focal ratio and focal length
parameters.value: f/1.3 Schmidt (doublet corrector, spherical mirror, S-YGH51 field flattener); 247
parameters.quote: articulating red and blue f/1.3 Schmidt cameras | an f/1.3 Schmidt camera with a doublet corrector, spherical mirror, a field-flattening lens of S-YGH51 glass
parameters.note: DERIVED: f_cam = 1.3 x 190 mm = 247 mm. (A web-search snippet of the AAT grating calculator, not saved, also gave 247 mm; not used as a source.) The detector sits inside the beam (a classical Schmidt camera: 'obstruction losses', S14 Sec. 1); the explorer's catadioptric 'mirror' camera drawing. Camera view: 8 deg off-axis angles; 230 mm aspheric doublet corrector plates (SH06 Sec. 2.3).

parameters.value: VPH transmission gratings, 20 mm thick, in the 190 mm beam, interchangeable; most with slanted fringes
parameters.quote: The VPH gratings were made by Ralcon Development Lab | All gratings are 20mm thick | most of the AAOmega gratings have their internal refractive index fringes slanted
parameters.note: The slant angles are NOT FOUND, so gTilt = 0. The grating is tilted slightly off Littrow to move the 0th-order ghost off the detector (SH06 Sec. 3.3: 'This ghost can be moved off the detector by tilting the grating').

parameters.value: each camera articulates; the camera angle sets the wavelength coverage
parameters.quote: The wavelength coverage for a particular grating angle is determined by the camera angle, which must hence be adjustable
parameters.note: The range of camera angles is NOT FOUND in the saved sources. Camera-collimator angle for the preset: psi = 2 x grating angle (INFERRED: the published central wavelengths equal the Littrow wavelengths 2 sin(alpha) / G to 0.0-0.6% at all five grating angles with a published center, see the settings table). The explorer's transmission 'trans' type at its symmetric Bragg setting needs no psi.

parameters.note: Not entered. No published setting with a coverage for any of them in the saved sources.

parameters.quote: All gratings are 20mm thick
parameters.note: gLen is left unset: the 190 mm beam at 47 deg has a 279 mm footprint (DERIVED, the explorer's Lg for 1700D), and the clear aperture is NOT FOUND.

parameters.parameter: Standard dichroic (x5700): cut and which arm reflects
parameters.value: cross-over 570 nm; blue (< 570 nm) reflected to the blue arm, red transmitted
parameters.loc: SH06 Sec. 2.3, Sec. 5.8, Fig. 1; C17 Sec. 2; H13 Sec. 2
parameters.quote: Only a single beam-splitter, with crossover at 570nm, is currently in use | We used the x5700 dichroic, which splits the arms at 5700 Å | poor dichroic performance on reflection
parameters.note: INFERRED which arm reflects: SH06 Sec. 5.8 blames, for the blue arm's low sensitivity, 'poor dichroic performance on reflection', so the blue arm is the reflected one; Fig. 1 shows the transmittance curve (about 1% below the edge, 95-98% above), so the red passes. The split sits in the collimated beam.

parameters.value: about 15 nm (10% to 90%), measured at normal incidence
parameters.quote: Response of the 570nm dichroic currently available for use with AAOmega. Note the abrupt transition region and generally smooth profile.
parameters.note: MEASURED from the figure (130 dpi render): 400 nm at pixel x = 399 and 1000 nm at x = 780 give 0.635 px/nm; the transmittance rises from 10% to 90% over about 10 px, 15 nm, centered near 610 nm. The curve is measured at NORMAL incidence ('Measured at Normal Incidence' in the legend), so its 50% point (about 610 nm) is not the working cross-over: the working angle shifts it to 570 nm. The explorer's w = 150 A (INFERRED to carry to the working angle, where the edge also narrows a little).

parameters.value: not published
parameters.note: A shift from the 610 nm normal-incidence edge to 570 nm corresponds to roughly 35-40 deg for a coating of effective index ~1.8 (INFERRED, order of magnitude only). For arms.js enter noAoi: true (as LLAMAS and 4MOST HRS), with 45 deg only for the drawing.

parameters.value: 670 nm cross-over (WiggleZ, from 2007 August; red 650-950 nm, blue 470-680 nm); selectable 570 or 670 nm (KOALA)
parameters.quote: The original AAOmega dichroic beam splitter cuts over at 570 nm while the new dichroic has a cut over at 670 nm | separated into blue and red arms using a dichroic beam splitter, selectable at 570 or 670 nm

parameters.value: one 2k x 4k E2V per arm (blue thinned 16 um silicon; red deep-depletion 40 um, low-fringing); long axis spatial; 15 um pixels
parameters.loc: SH06 Secs. 2.3, 2.3 (charge diffusion); H13 Sec. 2; Y15 Sec. 2
parameters.quote: a 2K x 4K E2V CCD with the long axis in the spatial direction | The DD silicon thickness is 40µm, vs 16µm for the blue arm CCD | an extra contribution from charge diffusion of order 1 pixel (15µm) | the detectors were two 2k×4k E2V CCDs. These detectors were replaced with new, cosmetically superior and more efficient 2k×4k E2V CCDs during 2014
parameters.note: Nx = 2048 along the dispersion, Ny = 4096 across, pix = 15 um. The pixel size is read from 'of order 1 pixel (15um)'. The 2014 replacement (both arms) keeps the format. CONFLICT: K26 says 'spectral dispersion occurs along the 4k axis', against SH06 (long axis spatial); the 3920-px fiber stack (10 px pitch x 392) and GAMA's 2100 A at 1 A/px settle it for 2048 along the dispersion.

parameters.quote: Wavelength coverage is 370 to 950nm and spectral resolution 1,000-8,000 in multi-Object mode, or 1,500-10,000 in IFU mode
parameters.note: Blue limit set by the 38 m fibers' transmission (D10 Sec. 4.1), red limit by the CCD response.

parameters.value: SPIRAL (512 fibers, Cassegrain); KOALA (1000 hexagonal microlenses, 0.7 or 1.25 arcsec sampling)
parameters.quote: the 512 fibre SPIRAL integral field unit (IFU) at Cassegrain focus | telecentric double-lenslet array comprising 1000 hexagonal microlenses
parameters.note: Not entered: the explorer's fiber model has no lenslet IFU feed; SH06 notes the IFU resolution is higher, 'due to the smaller projected fibre diameter'.

parameters.value: FWHM 3.1-3.3 px (blue), 3.3-3.6 px (red); design 3.2 px; typical ~3.4 px
parameters.quote: with actual FWHM in the range 3.1-3.3 pixels | giving 3.3-3.6 pixels | The cameras deliver largely Gaussian profiles of FWHM∼3.4 CCD pixels
parameters.note: DERIVED check (model): 140 um x 247 / 598.5 = 57.8 um = 3.85 px diameter; the explorer's equal-line-width slit is sqrt(3)/2 of it = 3.34 px, inside the published 3.1-3.6 px (not fitted: all inputs are sourced).

recommended_presets.name: AAT 3.9 m / AAOmega blue 580V
recommended_presets.why: The GAMA, WiggleZ and OzDES blue setup (H13, D11, D10, C17): the most used AAOmega grating (the survey workhorse, about 300 000 GAMA spectra), with R ~ 1300 over 3700-5800 A.

recommended_presets.name: AAT 3.9 m / AAOmega red 385R
recommended_presets.why: The matching red arm (385R, centered 7250 A): the pair gives continuous 3700-8800 A at R ~ 1000-1600 with the x5700 dichroic.

recommended_presets.name: AAT 3.9 m / AAOmega blue 1500V
recommended_presets.why: Medium resolution (R ~ 3700, Table 2); the grating angle 22.5 deg is from S14 Table 3; no published coverage, so only its dispersion is tested.

recommended_presets.name: AAT 3.9 m / AAOmega red 1000R
recommended_presets.why: Medium-resolution red (R ~ 3400): coverage 6280-7450 A, 1.9 A FWHM, R 3400 published (K26, SR07), an independent test.

not_found: A published optical layout figure of AAOmega: Smith et al. 2004 (SPIE 5492, 410; DOI 10.1117/12.551013; 2004SPIE.5492..410S) and Saunders et al. 2004 (SPIE 5492, 389; DOI 10.1117/12.550871; 2004SPIE.5492..389S) are behind the SPIE paywall and no preprint was found; SH06 has no layout figure.

The AAT/AAO AAOmega manual and grating calculator (aat.anu.edu.au/files/2dF-AAOmega-obs-manual_4.pdf; aat.anu.edu.au/cgi-bin/aaomega_calc.cgi): the AAT web site served only 'our website is offline awaiting patches for the recent PHP security issues' on 2026-11-18, so no manual was saved (the camera focal length 247 mm, the allowed camera-angle range 0-94.3 / 0-95.3 deg and the grating-angle range 0-49 deg, seen in a search snippet of the calculator, are therefore unverified).
Collimator focal length and camera focal length as stated lengths (both DERIVED from f-ratio x 190 mm).
Dichroic angle of incidence and any sentence stating that the collimator is on-axis or that the slit stands in the returning beam.
Distances: slit to collimator, collimator to grating, grating to camera, camera angle limits; grating clear apertures (gLen); fringe slant angles.
Fiber output focal ratio (the f/3.15 collimator speed is the design intent, L02 for the retired 2dF spectrographs and SH06).
Camera angle used for each published setting (psi = 2 x grating angle is INFERRED from the Littrow centers).
conflicts: Dispersion axis of the CCDs: SH06 Sec. 2.3 'with the long axis in the spatial direction' (and 392 spectra x 10 px = 3920 px; GAMA 2100 A at 1 A/px) against K26 Sec. 3 'spectral dispersion occurs along the 4𝑘 axis'. Adopted: 2048 px along the dispersion.

Dichroic cross-over: 570 nm (SH06, D10, Y15, K26) against '5700 A' (H13, D11, C17, 'x5700'): the same dichroic in nm and in A. D10 Table 6 gives its blue range as 370-580 nm, red 560-850 nm (overlap).
